items.stem: In GitHub Actions, what is the relationship between jobs in a single workflow by default?

options.text: Each job runs on its own fresh runner and they run in parallel unless a dependency is declared
options.rationale: Correct: jobs are isolated and parallel by default; needs declares ordering.

options.text: All jobs run as steps in one shared shell session
options.rationale: Steps share a runner within a job, but jobs are separate.

options.text: Jobs always run strictly in file order on one runner
options.rationale: Jobs are parallel unless ordered with needs.
Parallelism is the default when there is no dependency.

items.explanation: Correct: jobs are isolated and parallel by default; needs declares ordering.

items.stem: Which TWO practices improve the security of a GitHub Actions workflow?

options.text: Pinning third-party actions to a specific commit SHA or reviewed version
options.rationale: Correct: pinning prevents a moved tag from introducing unreviewed code.

options.text: Setting the workflow permissions to the least the jobs require
options.rationale: Correct: scoping GITHUB_TOKEN permissions limits what a compromised run can do.

options.text: Echoing secrets to the log to confirm their values
options.rationale: Printing secrets risks exposing them in logs.

options.text: Running untrusted fork pull requests with full secret access
options.rationale: Forked PRs should not receive privileged secrets.

options.text: Using a single personal access token with admin scope everywhere
options.rationale: A broad shared token violates least privilege.

items.explanation: Correct: pinning prevents a moved tag from introducing unreviewed code.

items.stem: How do you ensure a test workflow actually blocks a merge when it fails?

options.text: Configure it as a required status check in branch protection
options.rationale: Correct: branch protection with required checks enforces that the workflow must pass to merge.

options.text: Add a comment asking reviewers to check it
options.rationale: A comment does not enforce anything automatically.

options.text: Name the workflow 'required' in the YAML
options.rationale: The file name does not enforce merge rules.

options.text: Run the workflow only on a schedule
options.rationale: A scheduled run does not gate pull-request merges.

items.explanation: Correct: branch protection with required checks enforces that the workflow must pass to merge.
